parameters.query:
-- The channel decides the client (and so the GHL account), never the AI. An unknown channel, or a removed client's
-- (the bot should have left it), still returns one
-- row, of nulls, so the next step can raise the alert. A message from the agency's own staff (active members of the
-- staff list) returns no row, which ends the run quietly: the agency talking, not the client.
-- Values in order: 1 channel, 2 Slack user
select c.client_key, c.display_name, c.location_id,
       coalesce((select array_agg(o.display_name order by o.display_name)
                 from client_map o where o.channel_id <> $1), '{}') as other_client_names
from (select 1) as one
left join client_map c on c.channel_id = $1 and c.status <> 'removed'
where not is_staff($2);

parameters.text: =:warning: A message arrived in <#{{ $('Read message').first().json.channel_id }}> (`{{ $('Read message').first().json.channel_id }}`), which isn't linked to a current client in `client_map` (unknown, or the client was removed: remove the bot from that channel). No ticket was made, and the message isn't shown here.

parameters.query:
-- One statement: a reply in a known ticket's thread is added to that ticket; anything else opens a new ticket.
-- A message Slack delivers twice matches a unique key and returns no row, so the workflow stops there.
-- Values in order: 1 channel, 2 thread, 3 message key (channel:ts), 4 client key, 5 location, 6 text, 7 Slack user
with existing as (
  select id, text, slack_event_id from tickets where channel_id = $1 and thread_ts = $2
),
new_ticket as (
  insert into tickets (slack_event_id, channel_id, thread_ts, client_key, location_id, text)
  select $3, $1, $2, $4, $5, $6
  where not exists (select 1 from existing)
  on conflict do nothing
  returning id, text
),
follow_up as (
  insert into ticket_messages (ticket_id, slack_key, slack_user, text)
  select id, $3, $7, $6 from existing
  where slack_event_id <> $3  -- the opening message delivered again is not a follow-up
  on conflict (slack_key) do nothing
  returning ticket_id
),
saved as (
  select id as ticket_id, 'new' as kind, text as full_text from new_ticket
  union all
  -- The whole conversation so far for the agent: opening message, earlier follow-ups, then this one.
  select e.id, 'follow_up',
         e.text
         || coalesce((select string_agg(E'\n\nFollow-up from the client:\n' || m.text, '' order by m.created_at)
                      from ticket_messages m where m.ticket_id = e.id), '')
         || E'\n\nFollow-up from the client:\n' || $6
  from follow_up f join existing e on e.id = f.ticket_id
)
select s.ticket_id, s.kind, s.full_text,
       (select d.status from drafts d where d.ticket_id = s.ticket_id order by d.created_at desc limit 1) as last_status
from saved s;

parameters.query:
-- Before any AI call: may this client have another draft? (per-client limit per 60 minutes, migration 008)
select * from claim_draft_slot($1);

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ticket_id: $('Save message').first().json.ticket_id, client_key: $('Find client').first().json.client_key, location_id: $('Find client').first().json.location_id, text: $('Save message').first().json.full_text, other_client_names: $('Find client').first().json.other_client_names }) }}

parameters.query:
-- No draft: the agent didn't answer within 90 s, was busy (503) or failed. A person takes it (Post card posts it).
insert into drafts (ticket_id, draft, status)
values ($1::uuid, jsonb_build_object('error', $2::text), 'agent_unavailable')
returning id as draft_id, ticket_id, status, draft;

-- Remember where this draft's card sits, and mark the ticket's older open drafts "replaced" (they can no longer be
-- approved). Returns the older cards, so the next step can cross them out in Slack.
with card as (
  update drafts set queue_ts = $2 where id = $1::uuid returning id, ticket_id, created_at
),
replaced as (
  update drafts d set status = 'replaced'
  from card
  where d.ticket_id = card.ticket_id and d.id <> card.id
    and d.created_at < card.created_at and d.status in ('pending', 'agent_unavailable', 'limit_reached', 'client_paused')
  returning d.queue_ts
)
select queue_ts from replaced where queue_ts is not null;

parameters.blocksUi: ={{ JSON.stringify({ blocks: [{ type: "section", text: { type: "mrkdwn", text: ":arrows_counterclockwise: *Replaced by a newer draft.* The client added more to this ticket; use the newest card." } }] }) }}

parameters.query:
-- Over the client's hourly limit: no AI call. A person takes it from the "limit reached" card.
insert into drafts (ticket_id, draft, status)
values ($1::uuid, jsonb_build_object('limit', $2::integer), 'limit_reached')
returning id as draft_id, ticket_id, status, draft;

parameters.query:
-- A paused client (admin app): no draft slot and no AI call. A person answers by hand from the "paused" card.
-- Values in order: 1 ticket, 2 pause reason
insert into drafts (ticket_id, draft, status)
values ($1::uuid, jsonb_build_object('paused', $2::text), 'client_paused')
returning id as draft_id, ticket_id, status, draft;

-- Is the client paused? Read again here, after the ticket is saved, not taken from Find client: a pause made in
-- between still gets the "paused" card. Always one row. A client removed meanwhile comes back as "removed" and
-- goes on to the agent, whose own fresh key lookup refuses it before any AI call (a split-second case, accepted).
-- Values in order: 1 channel
select c.status, c.pause_reason from (select 1) as one left join client_map c on c.channel_id = $1;
